final_answer: Imagine a small coastal town where every summer, ice cream sales and shark attacks both rise. A local might conclude, "Eating ice cream causes shark attacks!" But this ignores a hidden factor: heat. On hot days, more people buy ice cream and also swim in the ocean, increasing the chance of shark encounters. The real cause is the weather, not the ice cream. This shows correlation (ice cream and sharks rising together) doesn't mean causation (one doesn't cause the other). Safe.
